title: Composing Two Functions in Both Orders
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Define the composition of two functions, then compute (f circle g)(x) and (g circle f)(x) for f(x) = x^2 and g(x) = 2x + 1, and compare the results.
finalAnswer: $(f \circ g)(x) = (2x+1)^2 = 4x^2 + 4x + 1$, while $(g \circ f)(x) = 2x^2 + 1$; composition is not commutative.

steps.title: State the Definition
steps.explanation: The composition f circle g means: feed x into g first, then feed the result g(x) into f. The domain of f circle g is the set of x for which g(x) lies in the domain of f.
steps.why: Knowing which function runs first prevents the most common composition error.

steps.title: Compute f circle g
steps.explanation: Replacing the input of the squaring machine with the expression 2x + 1 gives (2x + 1)^2, which expands to 4x^2 + 4x + 1.
steps.why: Substitution into the outer formula is the mechanical heart of composition.

steps.title: Compute g circle f and Compare
steps.explanation: Doubling x^2 and adding 1 gives 2x^2 + 1. At x = 1, f circle g yields 9 while g circle f yields 3, so the two compositions are different functions. Order matters, unlike multiplication of numbers.
steps.why: A single disagreeing input proves the two orders are not equal in general.
